title: Minting has no precondition beyond the caller's role and the rate limit, so there is no pause switch to flip
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.1.1.1 makes an unusually candid statement about what is *not* checked: "Only the `RELAYER` role is allowed to call `mintUSDS`, enforced by the `onlyRole(RELAYER)` gate on the function; **there is no other precondition or active-state check**." A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.1.2.1.2.1.2.1 says the same for `burnUSDS`.

So the entire guard on Grove drawing on Sky's balance sheet is two things: **who is calling**, and **how much allowance remains**. There is no global paused flag, no circuit-breaker state, no emergency mode the contract consults.

That explains the shape of the Freezer Role. A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.1.1.4 defines it as "the emergency role that can remove a compromised Relayer" — not an entity that can pause the system, because there is nothing to pause. **Freezing the Grove Liquidity Layer is implemented as de-authorizing every actor who can act on it**, which is why the Diamond PAU needed the AdministeredAgent indirection (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.1.1.1.4.1.5) to make actor removal surgical.

The design is defensible: fewer state variables on the hot path means fewer ways for the guard itself to fail, and a role-based halt cannot be bypassed by a forgotten function that omits the pause modifier. But it has a specific consequence worth naming — **a freeze is not atomic across a role held by three multisigs** (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.1.2.2). Halting activity means removing each relayer, and until the last removal lands, some path remains live.

The Tokenized Treasury Instances are different: there the `PAUSER_ROLE` genuinely pauses contract operations (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.1.2.4). The Liquidity Layer's own controller has no equivalent.
description: The Artifact states explicitly that mintUSDS and burnUSDS have 'no other precondition or active-state check' — which is why the Freezer's power is to remove relayers rather than to halt the contract.
